dicas.texto: Which part of a fraction tells how many equal parts make one whole?
Look at the denominator, the number below the fraction bar, and use it to set the number of intervals.
For Dale's amount, focus on the number below the 10 in 10/9.
Enter the denominator of 10/9 in the division field and confirm the number of equal intervals.
What does the numerator count after the whole has been divided into equal parts?
Use the ninths on the line and count ten equal intervals from zero.
The point is just to the right of 1 because the numerator is one greater than the denominator.
Starting at zero, count ten ninth-sized intervals and place the marker at that position.
How many equal parts are needed when one whole is not split into smaller fractional parts?
Write Liz's whole amount as a fraction with one whole in the numerator and the same number in the denominator.
For 1 pound written as 1/1, use the number below the fraction bar.
Enter the denominator of 1/1 in Liz's division field and confirm the single equal interval.
Where is one whole located on a number line that starts at zero?
Find the mark halfway between 0 and 2, because that mark represents one whole pound.
Use the label 1 as the target rather than the endpoints 0 or 2.
Place the marker directly on the tick labeled 1.
On a number line, which point represents the greater quantity: the point farther left or farther right?
Compare the locations of Dale's point and Liz's point relative to the mark labeled 1.
A fraction with a numerator greater than its denominator represents more than one whole.
Choose the sauce whose marked point is farther to the right on the number line.
Before submitting, check that your choice matches the sauce with the point farther to the right.
Review the selected comparison choice and then use the submission control.
Your selected choice should state that Dale's sauce has more ground beef.
Keep Sauce made by Dale. selected and click the Done button to submit.

exercicio.statement:
Dale and Liz are each making their own spaghetti sauce, and are using different amounts of ground beef to make it. If you wanted your sauce to have more ground beef, whose sauce should you choose? Use the number line to find out.
Dale is using 10/9 pounds of ground beef.
Liz is using exactly 1 pound of ground beef.
Which sauce should you choose?
